name: Positive-Support Deletion Criterion
statement: Repeatedly delete a coordinate occurring on no remaining left side of a positive source system and delete every row whose right side meets it. The original system is feasible exactly when the retained system is feasible, and a retained witness extends continuously and rationally at rational inputs. If every retained row has a singleton right side, then the logarithmic coefficient domain is open and convex; when nonempty, $\mathcal A(C)\cong\mathbb R^{d_C}$.
proof: Restore deleted coordinate groups in reverse order, assigning each a value larger than the finitely many ratios required by rows removed at that step. For singleton right sides, logarithms turn every retained positive inequality into a linear strict inequality; combining these with the convex negative inequalities and projecting preserves convexity.
